page: Amazon Web Services g6.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated computing instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing a standard 4 GB allocation per virtual core. Graphic acceleration and parallel compute workloads are handled by a single dedicated NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU equipped with 22 GB of video memory. In addition, the instance includes 900 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show top-tier execution in AI inference tasks, driven by the NVIDIA L4 accelerator. Small 135M language model inference achieves 12,203.0 prompt processing tokens per second and 470.24 text generation tokens per second, both falling into the top ten percent of evaluated instances. For medium 7B parameter models, prompt processing delivers 2,190.32 tokens per second and generation reaches 53.34 tokens per second. Raw CPU compute scores are steady, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25 percent at 2,990.03 and multi-core score reaching 47,873.35. Hardware cryptographic acceleration is prominent, yielding 37,936.6 on PassMark CPU encryption tests.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the instance balances mid-tier GPU acceleration with dense general compute resources and high-speed local NVMe storage. While the 22 GB of VRAM accommodates smaller models and quantization-focused 70B parameter prompt processing at 36.03 tokens per second, it presents a memory capacity bottleneck for unquantized large models or massive batch sizes. The bundled 900 GB NVMe volume offers low-latency scratch space without incurring external storage overheads.

The AWS g6.8xlarge is suited for machine learning inference, medium-scale model fine-tuning, video processing, graphics rendering pipelines, and parallel data analysis that requires balanced compute and high-bandwidth local caching.
